bugs.what: The 'name it (stands down)' pacify ability doesn't always unlock a blocked path immediately — at Barrow Crypt naming the wight/rats instantly opened the north passage, but at The Waiting Bough naming the gray sergeant left the way 'locked' and still required a separate will/grace check afterward. Inconsistent payoff for the same-looking ability made it unclear what 'stood down' actually guarantees.
bugs.where: Barrow Crypt vs. The Waiting Bough (Thornwold)

bugs.what: Large outdoor wood/downs areas (Ashwood near the Vale, the Iron Downs approach to Cinderhall) have many similarly-described rooms (spoil, tailings, cairns) with directional exits that don't obviously connect back to the intended route, so it's easy to wander a few extra rooms before 'get your bearings' clarifies the path.

A handful of failed skill checks (e.g. 'go through before nerve fails' at the Hundred Gallery fall, 'shore the dike' at Fenmarch) raise the DC on retry, which is well-telegraphed, but the initial DC/modifier math shown before rolling doesn't always make the true odds obvious (e.g. DC 10 with +3 shown as 'roll 7+' is fine, but DC vs total-needed phrasing took a few tries to parse confidently).

confusions: Early on it wasn't clear that 'travel to a known place' only moves between visited landmark nodes, not arbitrary rooms, until the game explicitly called it out after the first two rooms.

Whether accepting the priest's blessing (opening the barrow) would conflict with a later promise to the reeve (sealing it) wasn't fully clear until both NPCs and the innkeeper were consulted — the game rewards asking everyone, but a first-time player could easily lock in a contradiction without knowing to ask around first.

The exact requirements for the final rite (3 hollows rested + Vale king rested + first Reeve's confession) were only fully spelled out via the `status` tool, not proactively surfaced — a player who never calls status could reach Marrowgate without realizing they were one step short.
suggestions: Make 'name it' pacification consistently either fully clear a blocked path or clearly state 'a check is still needed' in the same message, so players don't have to learn the exception by trial.

Add a lightweight 'you've been here before, the way back to X is...' hint when re-entering a previously visited overworld node during backtracking, to reduce reliance on the free 'get bearings' action.
Surface the endgame rite requirements (3 hollows / king rested / confession) proactively the first time a player reaches Act II, not only on-demand via status.

The companion approval/disapproval banter after nearly every choice is excellent flavor — consider a way to review a condensed 'relationship history' per companion, since regard changes accumulate fast and are easy to lose track of without repeatedly opening status.
